fields.Frequency: 2–5 closures per store per year; region-wide events affect 20–60 stores simultaneously
fields.Participants: Regional Manager, Store Manager, VP Store Operations, HR, Security
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 3+ in store area, local government evacuation order, or facility safety assessment
fields.Volume: Up to 200 stores for nationwide super typhoons

Automation Opportunity: - System rule-based authorization of "authorizes closure with VP Store Operations approval for multi-store events" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of store status to "Temporarily Closed" on the store locator (replaces manual Step 3 posting).
Controls: - CTL-437 (ensure controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2).)
- operational: Regional Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Liability**: Customer or employee injury during closure process
- **Revenue loss**: PHP 840K+ per store per day of closure (avg PHP 25M/month ÷ 30)
System Touchpoints: - Store status management with automated channel propagation
- POS Z-report for mid-day closure
- Ecommerce/BOPIS order suspension per store
- Google Business Profile API for hours update

- **Custody & precedence** (per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md), E-02): this workflow is the closure-*decision* canon (Regional Manager decides; VP Store Operations approves multi-store events; COO chain-wide); closure/reopening *mechanics* and reporting run VS-26 W850, protocol context VS-26 W848; frequency canon: 2–5/store/yr typhoon-signal closures vs W850's 5–10/store/yr all-cause closures

steps.activity: Regional Manager assesses conditions per decision matrix: PAGASA signal, local government advisory, road accessibility, staff safety, facility integrity; authorizes closure with VP Store Operations approval for multi-store events

Store Manager executes closure: announce to customers via PA system, complete current transactions, secure cash in safe, power down non-essential systems, engage alarm, lock facility, escort remaining customers out safely

System automatically updates store status to "Temporarily Closed" on ecommerce, BOPIS, Google Business, and customer-facing channels; pauses all pending BOPIS orders with automated customer notification

fields.Participants: DC Ops Manager, Warehouse Supervisor, Safety Officer, VP Supply Chain
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 3+ in DC area or facility flooding risk assessment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "checkpoint, stage all MHE" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "Safety Officer confirms all personnel evacuated" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-437 (ensure controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inventory loss**: Flooding at DC3 (Laguna — low-lying area) could damage PHP 500M+ in inventory
- **Recovery time**: DC may be non-operational for 3–7 days post-flooding for cleanup and stock verification
System Touchpoints: - WMS emergency shutdown mode with transaction freeze
- Warehouse inventory location tracking for flood-risk assessment
- Security camera remote access

steps.activity: DC Ops Manager initiates emergency shutdown: halt all inbound/outbound operations, complete in-process picking/packing or secure at last checkpoint, stage all MHE (forklifts, reach trucks) at high ground, secure dock doors with flood barriers

Warehouse Supervisors execute critical asset protection: move high-value inventory (power tools, appliances) above flood line, seal chemical storage areas, secure server room with waterproof covers, activate UPS for graceful system shutdown
Safety Officer confirms all personnel evacuated; DC Ops Manager reports final status to Operations Center; maintains remote monitoring via security cameras where possible

fields.Participants: Logistics Mgr, DC Ops, Procurement, Store Ops, Government/NGO Liaison
fields.Trigger: Post-typhoon needs assessment or government/NGO emergency order

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-dispatch of "Supply Chain receives post-disaster needs assessment from affected stores" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Logistics Manager dispatches available trucks" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "count only, detailed matching deferred 48 hrs" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-437 (ensure controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Road inaccessibility**: Blocked roads delay emergency deliveries by 24–72 hours
- **Security**: Emergency deliveries in disaster zones face looting risk
System Touchpoints: - Emergency PO and transfer order creation with fast-track approval
- WMS priority wave management
- TMS dynamic routing considering road closures

steps.activity: Supply Chain receives post-disaster needs assessment from affected stores and regional government; prioritizes dispatch: medical facility orders first, then essential supply stores, then general replenishment
DC Ops picks emergency orders with dedicated priority wave; Logistics Manager dispatches available trucks (owned fleet first, then 3PL surge); coordinates road access with local government
Store Ops receives emergency delivery with expedited GR process (visual count only, detailed matching deferred 48 hrs); updates inventory; begins emergency sales operations

fields.Participants: COO, VP Store Operations, VP Supply Chain, CIO, CHRO, CFO, CMO, VP Legal
fields.Trigger: Multi-store/multi-DC typhoon impact event (Signal No. 3+ across 10+ stores)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "Center at HQ" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Functional leads provide situation reports" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documents all decisions for post-event review" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-437 (ensure controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2).)
- operational: COO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Information gaps**: Communication blackouts in severely affected areas delay damage assessment
- **Decision fatigue**: Extended events (48+ hours) strain leadership capacity
System Touchpoints: - Real-time dashboard: store/DC status, employee check-in, inventory levels, financial exposure
- Emergency communication platform with redundancy (internet + SMS + radio)
- Insurance claim notification system

steps.activity: COO activates Disaster Operations Center at HQ (Davao) or virtual: establishes command structure, communication channels, situation reporting cadence (every 2 hours during active event); assigns functional leads

Functional leads provide situation reports: Store Ops (store status, damage, employee safety), Supply Chain (DC status, inventory, logistics), IT (system status, communication channels), HR (employee welfare), Finance (financial exposure), Legal (regulatory/liability)

COO makes operational decisions: store closure/reopening, emergency procurement authorization (up to PHP 200M), staff redeployment, customer communication, insurance notification; documents all decisions for post-event review

fields.Frequency: 15–30 power outage activations per year across network
fields.Participants: Maintenance Staff, Store Manager, DC Ops Manager, Facilities
fields.Trigger: Commercial power outage at store or DC during/after typhoon

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logs activation time" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitors generator fuel consumption and arranges refueling logistics" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalates if runtime < 4 hours remaining" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-437 (ensure controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fuel scarcity**: Regional fuel shortages post-typhoon limit generator runtime
- **Generator failure**: Aging units at older stores may fail during extended runs
System Touchpoints: - IoT generator monitoring (fuel level, runtime, load status)
- POS offline mode activation
- Facilities management system for generator fleet tracking

- **Custody & precedence** (per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md), E-04): this workflow owns DC-level power contingency and typhoon-specific fuel logistics; store-level generator operations (any cause) run VS-24 W1223, the store canon
Time Estimate: - 30 min activation; ongoing monitoring every 4 hours during outage

steps.activity: Maintenance activates backup generator: verifies fuel level (minimum 8-hour runtime), starts generator, transfers load to backup, prioritizes circuits (POS, security, lighting, refrigeration for DC); logs activation time
Store Manager confirms POS operation in offline mode; switches to cash-first tender policy if connectivity lost; monitors generator fuel consumption and arranges refueling logistics
Facilities tracks generator runtime, fuel consumption, and maintenance status across affected locations; coordinates fuel resupply with suppliers; escalates if runtime < 4 hours remaining

fields.Frequency: 3–5 events per year requiring welfare tracking
fields.Participants: HR Ops Mgr, Store Managers, DC Ops, CHRO, Employee Relations

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "HR Ops activates welfare check" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinates relief goods distribution from store inventory per company policy" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracks overtime and hazard pay eligibility per DOLE advisory" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Employee trauma**: Psychological impact on staff in severely affected areas; requires counseling support
- **Staffing gaps**: Inability to reopen stores promptly due to staff displacement
System Touchpoints: - HR emergency notification with two-way status tracking
- Payroll emergency advance module
- Workforce scheduling with disaster redeployment
Time Estimate: - Initial welfare check: 12–24 hours; ongoing support: 1–4 weeks

steps.activity: HR Ops activates welfare check: automated SMS/IVR check-in to all employees in affected region; tracks response status (safe, affected, unreachable); Store/DC Managers supplement with direct calls to non-responders within 12 hours

For affected employees: HR assesses needs (housing, medical, financial); activates emergency salary advance (up to PHP 20,000 tax-free); coordinates relief goods distribution from store inventory per company policy
HR deploys replacement staff from unaffected stores to maintain minimum operations at reopened locations; tracks overtime and hazard pay eligibility per DOLE advisory

fields.Participants: Procurement Mgr, Merchandising, Finance, Logistics, Vendors
fields.Trigger: Post-disaster demand surge or government/NGO emergency procurement request

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow notification of "contacts key emergency vendors" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "tracks emergency vendor payments" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "Logistics arranges expedited transport" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-437 (ensure controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2).)
- operational: DTI enforcement and long-term vendor relationships
Pain Points / Risks: - **Price gouging**: Vendors increase prices during emergencies; mitigated by DTI enforcement and long-term vendor relationships
- **Quality risk**: Emergency procurement bypasses normal QC inspection; mitigated by CTL-437 (controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2))
System Touchpoints: - Emergency PO creation with fast-track approval workflow
- AP emergency payment processing
- TMS expedited routing

steps.activity: Procurement contacts key emergency vendors (tarps, plywood, nails, waterproofing, generators): confirms availability, negotiates emergency pricing (within DTI price freeze limits), secures allocation priority over competitors

Finance fast-tracks emergency vendor payments: bypasses standard 30-day terms for COD/advance payment to secure allocation; CFO authorizes emergency procurement budget (tiered: PHP 10M / Finance Controller; PHP 50M / CFO; PHP 200M / CEO)
Logistics arranges expedited transport: bypasses DC for direct-to-store delivery where possible; coordinates vendor truck dispatch to hardest-hit stores

fields.Trigger: Sudden weather deterioration while store is open with customers present
fields.Volume: Up to 200 stores; varies by typhoon track

workflows.name: Active Typhoon Customer Safety & In-Store Emergency Protocol

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitors weather conditions" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "updates every 15 minutes" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document any customer incidents for insurance and liability purposes" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-437 (ensure controlled execution — Active Disaster Response & Emergency Operations (PA-69.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer panic**: Large crowds during sudden severe weather create stampede risk
- **Liability exposure**: Customer injury on premises during weather emergency
System Touchpoints: - PA system with pre-recorded emergency announcements
- First aid station inventory tracking
- Incident reporting module for customer injury documentation

- **Custody & precedence** (per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md), E-03): the Store Manager holds site-level incident command at all times; the closure decision (Signal 3+/LGU order) follows W2510; evacuation protocol upkeep per VS-24 W695
Time Estimate: - Duration of event (typically 1–6 hours for shelter-in-place scenarios)

steps.activity: Store Manager monitors weather conditions; at sudden deterioration: activates customer safety protocol via PA announcement; directs customers away from outdoor lumber yard, loading dock, and exterior areas
If shelter-in-place required: guide customers to interior secure area (away from large windows, overhead fixtures); provide water, first aid; maintain calm with regular PA updates every 15 minutes
When safe to do so: gradually resume operations or execute orderly closure (W2510); document any customer incidents for insurance and liability purposes
